highlights.text: Al-Rāghib glosses ṣayāṣī as fortresses.
one single root sense, which he glosses as being stunned or struck dumb
yā la-l-bahītati, which he explains as meaning "O what a lie!"
a single core meaning: something striking or befalling a thing in a way that is unpleasant
dawāhī al-dahr ("the calamities of fate")
a thing cracking or fracturing without breaking fully into two separate pieces
a verse likens a curved object to a silver bracelet (dumluj)
a sound root whose meaning is opening out and parting
Al-fajj is a wide road.
a single core sense: covering and concealment
al-ghiṭāʾ ("the cover/covering") is defined as whatever a person covers himself with.
one core notion: turning/advancing toward something combined with submission — being led.
ahṭaʿa (used absolutely, without an object) — he/it hastened.
form a word denoting a shout or loud call.
Ibn Fāris glosses it as equivalent to halumma, i.e. "come" / "come here"
a single unified sense: humiliation combined with being turned away / repelled from something
God turns him away (ṣarafahu) and humiliates him (adhallahu)
al-kāhin, "the soothsayer" or "diviner" — one who claims to know hidden or future things.
loathing and foulness — detestation (shanāʾa) combined with ugliness or repulsiveness (qubḥ)
maqatahu, verbal noun maqt ("he loathed/detested him")
a single sound root whose core meaning is throwing or casting away
to throw something, to cast it from one's hand
al-nafʿ ("benefit") is that by which one attains good things (al-khayrāt)
describes someone shrinking back (أَحْجَمَ) from something out of fear and cowardice — i.e., recoiling or retreating
a single idea: habitually frequenting a place and returning to it
a line of Abū Dhuʾayb using نَوْب (nawb) in the sense of a recurring cause
a single sound root whose meaning centers on obedience and religious good
obedience/devotion (الطاعة)
two distinct roots: one meaning fear, the other meaning fineness/thinness and lightness
الرَّهْبَة is fear or dread.
a single root whose core idea is iḍṭirāb — shaking, agitation, unsteady motion
Used of the earth quaking (رَجَفَتِ الأَرْضُ)
a single small root whose core idea is a giving at an appointed time (عطاء لوقت)
الرِّزْق (al-rizq) is God's gift.
Two distinct senses under this root
al-suḥq — distance/remoteness.
pouring something out
سَكَبَ الْمَاءَ (sakaba al-mā'a) — "he poured the water."
a single core sense: bewilderment or disorientation (ḥayra)
a trackless open wasteland or desert
the letters t-y-n do not form a genuine derivational root
the word tīn ("fig")
a line of poetry (speaker unnamed) describing tawny, thirsty she-camels
One core meaning: the extension and spreading-out of a thing
al-thuʿbān — the large, long snake
a line of poetry comparing a winding track to a thuʿbān
a single sound root whose core sense is offspring and progeny
وَلَد (walad) — "child, offspring."
